question:
B. Is this measure already running in Åland (or in the Tyks university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure reduce deaths among the people it reaches, and by how much?
Measure: Smoking cessation started at the first specialist visit. Every current smoker with suspected lung cancer gets cessation medication and counselling at the first visit, as part of preparing for curative treatment.
effect_summary_en: In a Moscow cohort of 517 current smokers with early-stage NSCLC, quitting after diagnosis was linked to lower all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.53–0.85).
supported_en: Quitting after diagnosis was linked to an adjusted HR of 0.67 for all-cause mortality (Annals of Internal Medicine, 2021).
not_supported_en: The evidence is observational and does not show the effect of a first-visit programme itself, or any effect on whether patients become fit for surgery.
in_use_summary_en: Tyks has a smoking-cessation nurse at its lung clinic whom patients can contact. No public page shows cessation medication and counselling started at the first visit for every smoker with suspected lung cancer, at ÅHS or at Tyks.
summary_en: Tyks lists a smoking-cessation nurse at its lung clinic, but no public page from ÅHS or Tyks shows that every smoker with suspected lung cancer starts cessation treatment at the first specialist visit. An observational cohort in Annals of Internal Medicine (2021) found that quitting after an early-stage NSCLC diagnosis was linked to an adjusted all-cause mortality HR of 0.67 (95% CI 0.53–0.85), the same as the size we assume.
unanswered_en: No ÅHS page about cessation treatment for lung cancer patients was found; only a general ÅHS quit-smoking guide (PDF) turned up in a search, and it was not read.
